content.text:
You are reviewing a design proposal for the Lobu codebase (a Bun monorepo; the product is "Lobu", an agent platform where "Behaviors" are automations that run against real external data). Your job: give a brutally honest opinion on whether the proposal is OVERENGINEERED, and what the minimal viable version is. Be specific. Do NOT write code. Read-only — do not modify anything.

CONTEXT — the existing state (all verified true):
1. There is a working in-product "replay eval" engine in packages/server/src/runs/ (eval-runs.ts, eval-cases.ts, eval-scores.ts, eval-suite.ts) and a scorer queue (scheduled/score-eval-runs.ts). Flow: a real Behavior run is "promoted" into a $eval_case DB entity (source_run_id + human "expectation"), then replayed as a behavior_eval run under capture mode (executionMode='capture' signed token claim — the agent does the same reads but records side effects to runs.dry_run_preview instead of performing them), then scored by code metrics (completed_window, output_present) + an optional LLM judge against the expectation. A suite runner replays each case N trials (default 3) and readEvalResults compares latest-vs-previous trial-group means, flagging a regression only when the drop exceeds the case's observed spread. Three HTTP routes exist: POST /api/:orgSlug/agents/evals/cases, POST .../behaviors/:behaviorId/evals/run, GET .../behaviors/:behaviorId/evals/results. Integration tests green. BUT: no UI, no ClientSDK methods, no committed eval corpus, no CI gate. The only trigger surfaces are the raw HTTP routes and two ad-hoc bun scripts (scripts/promote-eval-case.ts, scripts/queue-eval-run.ts) whose headers explicitly say the trigger surface "has not had design sign-off".
2. There is also a promptfoo provider (packages/promptfoo-provider) that drives a Lobu agent through the gateway Agent API for conversational evals (committed promptfooconfig.yaml in examples/, but nothing in CI runs them; provider hardcodes dryRun:true on sessions).
3. The CLI (packages/cli) is commander-based and has a generic admin dispatcher: `lobu call <tool>` posts to POST /api/:orgSlug/:toolName, and GET /api/:orgSlug/tools lists the surface. Any tool registered on that surface is reachable from CLI, MCP clients, and the SDK.

THE PROPOSAL being reviewed ("evals as a first-party primitive", corpus-as-code layer over the existing replay engine):
- Register eval actions on the admin tool surface (eval.promote_case, eval.run_suite, eval.read_results, eval.export_case) so CLI/SDK/MCP reach them with no bespoke wiring.
- `lobu eval` subcommands: init (scaffold agents/<id>/evals/ dirs), export <run-id> (promote a real run and dump it to a committed YAML file containing the frozen dispatch payload + expectation + judge_model + case_key + provenance source_run), validate (dry-run parse), apply (idempotent sync of committed YAML files into $eval_case entities), run (queue suite), results (read), check (exit non-zero if any case regressed beyond its spread — the CI gate).
- The committed YAML file is SELF-CONTAINED (carries the full frozen dispatch payload), so cases survive runs-table pruning. Payload comes from exporting real runs, not hand-authoring.
- Server deltas: (a) createEvalRunFromPayload mint (payload instead of sourceRunId) + a code:<caseId> identity scheme; (b) a sync/upsert endpoint for apply; (c) export needs the frozen payload returned from a route (not currently exposed); (d) surfacing readEvalResults' existing regression-vs-spread logic as the `check` gate.
- SDK verbs: client.behaviors.evals.promote/run/results.
- Owletto UI later (a Behavior detail tab showing per-case latest/previous/spread).

THE QUESTION: Is this overengineered? Where would you cut? What is the minimum that makes "evals as code" actually usable and CI-gated, and is the replay-engine-as-first-party-primitive framing right vs just leaning on promptfoo? Think about: is the self-contained payload file necessary or is a source_run pointer enough? Is the admin-tool registration + SDK + CLI + UI four surfaces too many? Is the whole corpus-as-code layer premature when there is no UI or SDK for the engine at all yet? Give a clear verdict: overengineered / right-sized / under-scoped, then a concrete minimal cut.

I’m using the Lobu operator guidance because this is a repo-specific architecture review with public-surface and database-contract boundaries. I’ll inspect the current implementation and relevant repo guidance read-only, then give a hard cut rather than designing from the proposal alone.

The repo confirms the key product boundary: a new admin tool or SDK verb is not “free plumbing”; it is a public API decision. I’m separating what CI genuinely needs from what merely increases discoverability, and checking whether the proposed frozen payload is stable enough to deserve a committed format.

Two design problems are now clear. First, the proposed YAML is not actually self-contained: the “frozen payload” still contains deployment-local Behavior/version/agent/event references and relies on the workspace data remaining available. Second, the existing latest-versus-previous reader cannot safely become a CI gate without correlating the exact queued batch and failing closed on missing or incomparable results.

## Verdict

**Overengineered as a V1—and under-scoped where CI correctness actually matters.**

The replay engine is worth making first-party. But the proposal bundles five separate projects: public API design, CLI UX, corpus synchronization, payload archival, and statistical CI gating. The archival and extra surfaces arrive before anyone has proved that teams will maintain these eval cases.

More importantly, the proposed `check` is not yet a trustworthy CI gate.

## The hard problems the proposal misses

- `runEvalSuite` only queues work. Scoring waits at least 60 seconds and is scheduled every five minutes, so a naïve `run && check` can read old results for several minutes. See [score-eval-runs.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/scheduled/score-eval-runs.ts:47) and [jobs.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/scheduled/jobs.ts:387).

- Results have no suite or commit identity. Concurrent CI jobs can reuse or interleave trials. `check` must correlate the exact run IDs returned by its own invocation, not assume that the newest positional scores belong to it.

- Missing evidence currently looks healthy. A first-ever suite has no `previous`; a changed metric set produces `delta = null`; an unscored case has no regression. A CI gate must fail closed on empty, skipped, incomplete, timed-out, unscored, or incomparable cases.

- “Drop exceeds latest spread” is too weak for CI. Previous `[1,1,1]` and current `[0,0,1]` produces a 0.667 drop but a spread of 1, so it is not flagged. One flaky trial can mask a major regression. The existing logic is reasonable dashboard evidence, but not sufficient as the sole merge gate. See [eval-suite.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/runs/eval-suite.ts:360).

- Regression-only gating permits permanently bad behavior: `0 → 0` passes. Committed cases need an absolute policy such as required protocol metrics and/or `min_score`; historical regression should initially be supplemental.

## The frozen payload is not self-contained

Do not commit raw `approved_input` in V1.

It removes dependence on the source `runs` row, but still contains deployment-local references: Behavior ID, Behavior-version ID, agent ID, event IDs, connection IDs, and time windows. Connector trigger payloads can also include real `input_text`, making accidental PII/customer-data commits plausible. Workspace triggers remain pointers into the append-only event store. See [queue-service.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/runs/queue-service.ts:50) and [behavior-triggers.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/connector-sdk/src/behavior-triggers.ts:126).

So it is a **run-row-independent replay manifest**, not a self-contained fixture. It will not be portable to another org or clean CI environment, and accepting client-supplied dispatch payloads creates a substantial validation and tenancy boundary.

For V1, a `source_run_id` pointer is enough if:

- evals run against one long-lived test workspace;
- promoting a case pins that source run against pruning;
- broken pointers fail validation/check loudly.

If portable eval fixtures become a proven requirement, design a versioned, redacted, server-produced snapshot format separately. Do not expose the internal dispatch payload as that format.

## Minimal viable cut

Use one canonical `manage_evals` admin tool with action variants, matching the repo’s existing admin-tool pattern:

- `ensure_case` — idempotently create or update expectation/judge settings.
- `run_suite` — queue trials and return exact case/run IDs.
- `read_batch` — report terminal and scoring state for those exact run IDs, plus results.

The current promote fast path returns an existing case without updating its expectation, so “apply” semantics require a real ensure/upsert operation.

Then add only two CLI workflows:

- `lobu eval export <run-id>`: emit a small versioned manifest containing stable Behavior/agent slugs, `case_key`, `source_run_id`, expectation, judge model, trials, and an explicit CI threshold.
- `lobu eval check <manifest>`: parse, ensure cases, queue, wait for the exact returned run IDs, obtain their scores, print results, and exit non-zero on any incomplete or failed condition.

`check` already subsumes parsing, validation, apply, run, waiting, results, and exit-code behavior. Cut these from V1:

- `init`
- standalone `validate`
- standalone `apply`
- standalone `run`
- standalone `results`
- `createEvalRunFromPayload`
- `code:<caseId>` identity changes
- dedicated `client.behaviors.evals.*` verbs
- Owletto UI

Admin-tool registration already supplies REST, generated-client/OpenAPI access, generic `lobu call`, and named MCP dispatch while keeping admin tools out of normal agent discovery ([registry.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/server/src/tools/registry.ts:418)). Adding bespoke SDK verbs immediately would duplicate the contract.

For CI, `check` should fail on:

- zero active cases;
- any skipped case;
- any returned run not terminal and scored before timeout;
- missing expected judge metric;
- changed/incomparable metric signatures;
- required protocol metric failure or score below the committed threshold.

Keep latest-versus-previous/spread in the report. Do not make it the sole gate until there is explicit baseline-batch identity and concurrency handling.

## Replay engine versus promptfoo

The first-party direction is right, but call it a **first-party Behavior replay-eval lane**, not a general eval primitive.

Promptfoo tests conversational Agent API behavior: textual prompts, multi-turn exchanges, RAG/tool assertions, and model comparisons. Its `dryRun: true` session does not recreate a Behavior’s version-pinned trigger, real data window, completion protocol, or captured side effects ([provider.ts](/Users/burakemre/Code/lobu/packages/promptfoo-provider/src/provider.ts:209)).

Use both:

- Promptfoo for conversational agent evals—and wire the existing corpus into CI immediately if that is the current need.
- Lobu replay evals for scheduled/event-driven Behaviors operating on real workspace data.

Do not unify them yet. The minimal replay release should prove that people actually export, maintain, and gate Behavior cases before Lobu takes ownership of a portable corpus format and four user-facing surfaces.
